Codex review: needs real behavior proof before merge. _Reviewed August 24, 2026, 4:08 AM ET / 08:08 UTC._ # ClawSweeper review ## What this changes This PR adds profile-bound Gateway roles that cap cross-session access, allowed agents, and operator scopes for authenticated team users. ## Merge readiness ⛔ **Blocked until stronger real behavior proof is added - 11 items remain** Keep open: a role downgrade can retain an old admin scope through an awaited tool hook, and the documented identity-only setup has no safe first-maintainer bootstrap path. **Priority:** P1 **Reviewed head:** `6176265d0e83e99c68a581afbc75bf1c95f650ed` **Owner decision:** Required. See [Decision needed](#decision-needed). ## Review scores | Measure | Result | What it means | |---|---|---| | **Overall readiness** | 🦪 silver shellfish **(2/6)** | The broad role-policy implementation has useful coverage, but two high-impact authorization and setup defects remain unaddressed. | | **Proof confidence** | 🦐 gold shrimp **(3/6)** | Needs stronger real behavior proof before merge: Authority-chain proof required: the posted loopback trace proves reconnect-time revocation but not a role downgrade during an awaited hook; show the demoted operator is rejected before an admin Gateway final effect. After adding proof, update the PR body; ClawSweeper should re-review automatically. If it does not, the PR author or someone with repository write access can comment `@clawsweeper re-review`. | | **Patch quality** | 🦪 silver shellfish **(2/6)** | Security review found an item that needs attention. | ## Verification | Check | Result | Evidence | |---|---|---| | **Real behavior** | Needs proof | Needs stronger real behavior proof before merge: Authority-chain proof required: the posted loopback trace proves reconnect-time revocation but not a role downgrade during an awaited hook; show the demoted operator is rejected before an admin Gateway final effect. After adding proof, update the PR body; ClawSweeper should re-review automatically. If it does not, the PR author or someone with repository write access can comment `@clawsweeper re-review`. | | **Evidence reviewed** | 7 items | Stale authority after an await: Tool invocation awaits the before-tool hook, then installs the pre-await profile and scope snapshot as in-process authority. The dispatcher builds a synthetic client from that snapshot, and method authorization accepts a retained operator.admin scope without a current role-policy lookup.
Disconnect does not revoke retained synthetic authority: users.setRole invalidates and closes matching WebSocket clients, but the production disconnect path only mutates live clients; it cannot clear a previously-created synthetic tool client. The existing test simulates revocation by mutating a local scopes object rather than exercising that path.
Required authority proof remains absent: The in-process-dispatch test proves authority expires after an invocation completes, not that a role change during an awaited hook blocks an admin method before dispatch. The provided PR trace covers reconnect-time revocation, not this race. | | **Findings** | 2 actionable findings | [P1] Revalidate role scopes before in-process tool dispatch
[P1] Provide a non-escalating role bootstrap path | | **Security** | Needs attention | Role revocation does not reach retained tool authority: An awaited tool hook can outlive a user’s role downgrade while retaining the old `operator.admin` scope in a synthetic client; Gateway method routing trusts that stale scope before a privileged side effect. | ## How this fits together Gateway converts authenticated identity into operator scopes before routing WebSocket, HTTP, and tool requests. This change stores a role on the user profile and applies its ceiling across session and agent operations, including in-process tool calls. ```mermaid flowchart LR A[Verified user identity] --> B[Gateway authentication] B --> C[Profile role and scope ceiling] C --> D[WebSocket HTTP and tool requests] D --> E[Session and agent authorization] E --> F[Gateway side effects] ``` ## Decision needed | Question | Recommendation | |---|---| | Which safe bootstrap authority should an identity-only Gateway use to assign its first named role without granting every default guest operator.admin? | **Require an explicit scoped bootstrap path:** Add a narrowly bounded bootstrap authority or setup flow that can assign the first role without making the default role administrative. | Why: The feature’s least-privilege model cannot be made operable by a warning alone; choosing a bootstrap mechanism determines the public configuration and recovery contract. ## Before merge - [ ] **Add real behavior proof** - Needs stronger real behavior proof before merge: Authority-chain proof required: the posted loopback trace proves reconnect-time revocation but not a role downgrade during an awaited hook; show the demoted operator is rejected before an admin Gateway final effect. After adding proof, update the PR body; ClawSweeper should re-review automatically. If it does not, the PR author or someone with repository write access can comment `@clawsweeper re-review`. - [ ] **Revalidate role scopes before in-process tool dispatch (P1)** - A role downgrade during `runBeforeToolCallHook` leaves the retained AsyncLocal authority with its original scopes. The synthetic client then carries those scopes into method authorization, which accepts `operator.admin` without consulting the now-downgraded role. Closing the WebSocket only rejects buffered frames and does not revoke this in-process client, so a hook-delayed tool can still make an admin Gateway call after `users.setRole`. Re-resolve the role ceiling or generation immediately before the routed final effect and add the hook-race test. - [ ] **Provide a non-escalating role bootstrap path (P1)** - The documented configuration assigns every unassigned identity to `guest`, whose ceiling strips the identity’s `operator.admin` grant, while `users.setRole` is the only documented assignment path and itself requires that scope. An identity-only deployment using this example therefore cannot promote its first maintainer; putting admin in the default role instead grants it to every guest. Add a scoped bootstrap mechanism or reject activation until one is configured, and cover the trusted-proxy setup end-to-end. - [ ] **Resolve security concern: Role revocation does not reach retained tool authority** - An awaited tool hook can outlive a user’s role downgrade while retaining the old `operator.admin` scope in a synthetic client; Gateway method routing trusts that stale scope before a privileged side effect. - [ ] **Resolve merge risk (P1)** - The PR’s acknowledged sessions.patch owner-stamping gap can hide a role-capped user’s newly created session until its canonical repair is linked or landed. - [ ] **Resolve merge risk (P1)** - Exact-head CI remains in progress in the supplied context; it does not affect the two source-proven blockers. - [ ] **Complete next step (P2)** - Maintainers must choose the bootstrap contract and require the missing revocation-before-I/O proof before this cross-cutting role feature can merge. - [ ] **Improve patch quality** - Add a paused-hook role-downgrade test that proves an admin method is rejected before dispatch. - [ ] **Improve patch quality** - Choose and prove a safe first-maintainer bootstrap flow for trusted identity authentication. - [ ] **Improve patch quality** - Link or land the sessions.patch owner-stamping repair before claiming own-session access coverage. ## Findings - [P1] Revalidate role scopes before in-process tool dispatch — `src/gateway/server-plugin-in-process-dispatch.ts:161-195` - [P1] Provide a non-escalating role bootstrap path — `docs/gateway/configuration-reference.md:715-727` - [high] Role revocation does not reach retained tool authority — `src/gateway/server-plugin-in-process-dispatch.ts:161`
Agent review details ### Security Needs attention: The diff permits stale administrator authority to cross a role-revocation boundary into an in-process Gateway side effect. ### Review metrics | Metric | Value | Why it matters | |---|---|---| | **Role policy surface** | 1 config subtree added; 1 persisted nullable profile field; 1 Gateway role-assignment RPC added | This creates configuration, stored-state, and administrative contracts whose bootstrap and upgrade behavior must be safe. | | **Production and test LOC** | PR body reports approximately production +2.2k and tests +4.1k | The cross-entry-point authorization surface needs final-effect revocation proof beyond the current test coverage. | ### Stored data model Persistent data-model change detected: `database schema: docs/reference/database-schemas.md`, `database schema: src/state/user-profiles.test.ts`, `serialized state: src/gateway/agent-turn/agent-session-persist.test.ts`, `serialized state: src/gateway/session-create-service.ts`, `serialized state: src/gateway/session-group-defaults-access.ts`, `serialized state: src/gateway/session-group-mutation-targets.ts`, and 28 more. Confirm migration or upgrade compatibility proof before merge. ### Merge-risk options **Maintainer options:** 1. **Repair revocation and bootstrap before merge (recommended)** Fence each routed in-process effect with current role authority, add the awaited-hook demotion proof, and provide a least-privilege first-maintainer path. 2. **Pause the feature** Do not land team roles until maintainers choose and validate an operable bootstrap contract. ### Technical review Best possible solution: Add a non-escalating first-maintainer bootstrap path and revalidate live role authority immediately before each in-process final effect, with trusted-identity end-to-end proof for both. Do we have a high-confidence way to reproduce the issue? Yes, from source: pause the before-tool hook for an administrator, demote that profile through users.setRole, then resume a tool that dispatches an admin Gateway method; the retained synthetic client still carries the old scope. The bootstrap lockout follows directly from the documented guest ceiling and admin-only assignment method. Is this the best way to solve the issue? No. Closing a WebSocket is not a live authorization check for retained in-process clients, and a Doctor warning cannot bootstrap an administrator; use a current-policy fence plus a deliberate scoped bootstrap authority. Full review comments: - [P1] Revalidate role scopes before in-process tool dispatch — `src/gateway/server-plugin-in-process-dispatch.ts:161-195` A role downgrade during `runBeforeToolCallHook` leaves the retained AsyncLocal authority with its original scopes. The synthetic client then carries those scopes into method authorization, which accepts `operator.admin` without consulting the now-downgraded role. Closing the WebSocket only rejects buffered frames and does not revoke this in-process client, so a hook-delayed tool can still make an admin Gateway call after `users.setRole`. Re-resolve the role ceiling or generation immediately before the routed final effect and add the hook-race test. Confidence: 0.97 - [P1] Provide a non-escalating role bootstrap path — `docs/gateway/configuration-reference.md:715-727` The documented configuration assigns every unassigned identity to `guest`, whose ceiling strips the identity’s `operator.admin` grant, while `users.setRole` is the only documented assignment path and itself requires that scope. An identity-only deployment using this example therefore cannot promote its first maintainer; putting admin in the default role instead grants it to every guest. Add a scoped bootstrap mechanism or reject activation until one is configured, and cover the trusted-proxy setup end-to-end. Confidence: 0.96 Overall correctness: patch is incorrect Overall confidence: 0.95 AGENTS.md: found and applied where relevant. Codex review notes: model internal, reasoning high; reviewed against [23df5799fd01](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/23df5799fd01b8256c016f4a6d2924e68b46a322). ### Labels Label changes: - add `merge-risk: 🚨 auth-provider`: The role ceiling changes trusted-proxy and Tailscale identity authentication behavior, including whether their granted scopes survive. - add `rating: 🦪 silver shellfish`: Overall readiness is 🦪 silver shellfish; proof is 🦐 gold shrimp and patch quality is 🦪 silver shellfish. - remove `rating: 🧂 unranked krab`: Current PR rating is `rating: 🦪 silver shellfish`, so this older rating label is no longer current. Label justifications: - `P1`: The advertised team-role flow can either retain revoked admin authority or leave an identity-only deployment unable to assign its first maintainer. - `merge-risk: 🚨 compatibility`: Enabling the documented default role can remove an existing identity-granted admin scope with no operable upgrade path. - `merge-risk: 🚨 security-boundary`: A demoted operator can retain operator.admin in an in-process synthetic client after the role change. - `merge-risk: 🚨 auth-provider`: The role ceiling changes trusted-proxy and Tailscale identity authentication behavior, including whether their granted scopes survive. - `rating: 🦪 silver shellfish`: Overall readiness is 🦪 silver shellfish; proof is 🦐 gold shrimp and patch quality is 🦪 silver shellfish. - `status: 📣 needs proof`: The PR needs real behavior proof before ClawSweeper can clear the contributor ask. Needs stronger real behavior proof before merge: Authority-chain proof required: the posted loopback trace proves reconnect-time revocation but not a role downgrade during an awaited hook; show the demoted operator is rejected before an admin Gateway final effect. After adding proof, update the PR body; ClawSweeper should re-review automatically. If it does not, the PR author or someone with repository write access can comment `@clawsweeper re-review`. ### Evidence Security concerns: - [high] Role revocation does not reach retained tool authority — `src/gateway/server-plugin-in-process-dispatch.ts:161` An awaited tool hook can outlive a user’s role downgrade while retaining the old `operator.admin` scope in a synthetic client; Gateway method routing trusts that stale scope before a privileged side effect. Confidence: 0.97 Acceptance criteria: - [P1] Configure identity-only Gateway roles with a default guest and establish the first maintainer without giving guests operator.admin. - [P1] Pause a before-tool hook, demote the active profile, then verify an admin Gateway call is denied before its final effect. - [P1] Create and re-open a session through sessions.patch as a role-capped profile after the owner-stamping repair. What I checked: - **Stale authority after an await:** Tool invocation awaits the before-tool hook, then installs the pre-await profile and scope snapshot as in-process authority. The dispatcher builds a synthetic client from that snapshot, and method authorization accepts a retained operator.admin scope without a current role-policy lookup. ([`src/gateway/tools-invoke-shared.ts:394`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/6176265d0e83/src/gateway/tools-invoke-shared.ts#L394), [6176265d0e83](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/6176265d0e83)) - **Disconnect does not revoke retained synthetic authority:** users.setRole invalidates and closes matching WebSocket clients, but the production disconnect path only mutates live clients; it cannot clear a previously-created synthetic tool client. The existing test simulates revocation by mutating a local scopes object rather than exercising that path. ([`src/gateway/server-request-context.ts:368`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/6176265d0e83/src/gateway/server-request-context.ts#L368), [6176265d0e83](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/6176265d0e83)) - **Required authority proof remains absent:** The in-process-dispatch test proves authority expires after an invocation completes, not that a role change during an awaited hook blocks an admin method before dispatch. The provided PR trace covers reconnect-time revocation, not this race. ([`src/gateway/server-plugin-in-process-dispatch.authorization.test.ts:210`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/6176265d0e83/src/gateway/server-plugin-in-process-dispatch.authorization.test.ts#L210), [6176265d0e83](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/6176265d0e83)) - **Documented configuration locks out first role assignment:** The example gives the identity an admin grant but then applies a default guest role whose ceiling omits operator.admin; the only documented role-assignment method requires administrator scope. Adding admin to the default would instead grant it to all guests. Public docs: [`docs/gateway/configuration-reference.md`](https://docs.openclaw.ai/gateway/configuration-reference). ([`docs/gateway/configuration-reference.md:715`](https://docs.openclaw.ai/gateway/configuration-reference), [6176265d0e83](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/6176265d0e83)) - **Known session-owner gap affects the advertised role flow:** The sessions.patch creation path authorizes a missing entry and writes the projected entry without the canonical creation stamp, while catalog visibility treats createdActor as ownership. The PR body identifies this as a separate follow-up; no canonical repair is linked here. ([`src/gateway/server-methods/sessions-patch-engine.ts:197`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/6176265d0e83/src/gateway/server-methods/sessions-patch-engine.ts#L197), [6176265d0e83](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/6176265d0e83)) - **Current-main and release status:** Current main is 23df5799fd and does not contain src/gateway/operator-role-policy.ts; no version tag contains the PR head. The feature is therefore neither implemented on current main nor released. ([`src/gateway/operator-role-policy.ts`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/23df5799fd01/src/gateway/operator-role-policy.ts), [23df5799fd01](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/23df5799fd01)) Likely related people: - **steipete:** Grafted-head blame attributes the role-dispatch and role-configuration surface to this contributor. (role: current feature contributor; confidence: medium; commits: [6176265d0e83](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/6176265d0e83e99c68a581afbc75bf1c95f650ed); files: `src/gateway/server-plugin-in-process-dispatch.ts`, `src/gateway/server-request-context.ts`, `docs/gateway/configuration-reference.md`) ### Rating scale | Score | Internal tier | Crab rank | Meaning | |---:|:---:|---|---| | **6/6** | S | 🦀 challenger crab | Exceptional readiness | | **5/6** | A | 🦞 diamond lobster | Very strong readiness | | **4/6** | B | 🐚 platinum hermit | Good normal PR; ordinary maintainer review | | **3/6** | C | 🦐 gold shrimp | Useful, but confidence is limited | | **2/6** | D | 🦪 silver shellfish | Proof or implementation needs work | | **1/6** | F | 🧂 unranked krab | Not merge-ready | | N/A | NA | 🌊 off-meta tidepool | Rating does not apply | Overall follows the weaker of proof and patch quality. Shiny media proof means a screenshot, video, or linked artifact directly shows the changed behavior. Runtime, network, CSP, and security claims still need visible diagnostics. ### Workflow - ClawSweeper keeps one durable marker-backed review comment per issue or PR. - Re-runs edit this comment so the latest verdict, findings, and automation markers stay together instead of adding duplicate bot comments. - A fresh review can be triggered by eligible `@clawsweeper re-review` comments, exact-item GitHub events, scheduled/background review runs, or manual workflow dispatch. - PR/issue authors and users with repository write access can comment `@clawsweeper re-review` or `@clawsweeper re-run` on an open PR or issue to request a fresh review only. - Maintainers can also comment `@clawsweeper review` to request a fresh review only. - Fresh-review commands do not start repair, autofix, rebase, CI repair, or automerge. - Maintainer-only repair and merge flows require explicit commands such as `@clawsweeper autofix`, `@clawsweeper automerge`, `@clawsweeper fix ci`, or `@clawsweeper address review`. - Maintainers can comment `@clawsweeper explain` to ask for more context, or `@clawsweeper stop` to stop active automation. ### History
